ai_summary:
Scottish wind generation currently stands at an estimated 1.8 GW, operating at 17.8% of installed Scottish wind capacity while total GB wind output reaches 8.6 GW. Scotland’s clean power abundance is demonstrated by a regional carbon intensity of 0 gCO2/kWh, compared against 174 gCO2/kWh GB-wide. However, transmission bottlenecks continue to restrict energy transfer south, resulting in 578 MWh of Scottish generation curtailed so far today. Managing these local network constraints has driven Balancing Mechanism costs of about £38,660 today. To replace this lost clean power, an estimated 109,820 m3 of gas was burned elsewhere, discharging 202 tonnes of additional CO2. 

Extrapolating today's constraint costs produces an estimated total yearly curtailment cost of £14 million to the nearest million. While calculating the precise £/MWh increase across all UK consumer invoices would require total national demand figures excluded under strict reporting rules, today's constraint expenditure directly imposes an overhead of roughly £67/MWh on the curtailed energy itself. This ongoing friction illustrates how structural transmission deficits simultaneously elevate consumer energy bills and force fossil fuel reliance despite zero-carbon generation potential.
